accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let A be an m-element subset of G with m <= p < hm - h + 1. Is it true that the minimum possible size of the h-fold sumset hA is p, and that equality |hA| = p holds if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?
accepted.context_brief: Direct problem for ordinary h-fold sumsets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that m <= p < hm - h + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |hA| = rho(G, m, h) = p if, and only if, A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G with |H| = p.

accepted.question_text: In the boundary case where p is the smallest prime divisor of n and p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of a finite abelian group G for which the h-fold sumset hA has minimum possible size. In particular, beyond arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p, determine all subsets that can occur in this extremal case.

evidence.quote: This leaves the case when p = hm - h + 1, where arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets in a coset of a subgroup of order p are two of several possibilities. It may be an interesting problem to classify all such subsets.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume h < m <= p. Is the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset of an m-element subset always min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}? In other words, does rho_hat(G, m, h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1} hold throughout this range?
accepted.context_brief: Restricted sumset formula when m <= p

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 If p is the smallest prime divisor of n and h < m <= p, then rho_hat(G, m, h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume 2 <= h <= m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Classify the m-element subsets A of G whose h-fold restricted sumset has the minimum size hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that equality |h_hat A| = hm - h^2 + 1 occurs only in the exceptional case h = 2, m = 4 with A = {a, a + g1, a + g2, a + g1 + g2}, or when A is an arithmetic progression in G?
accepted.context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets above the prime threshold

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that 2 <= h <= m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |h_hat A| = hm - h^2 + 1 if, and only if, h = 2, m = 4, and A = {a, a + g1, a + g2, a + g1 + g2} for some a, g1, g2 in G, or A is an arithmetic progression in G.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume m <= p < hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that an m-element subset A satisfies |h_hat A| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?
accepted.context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets at size p

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that m <= p < hm - h^2 + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |h_hat A| = p if, and only if, A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G with |H| = p.

accepted.question_text: For an abelian group G of order n, compare the minimum size of a 2-fold signed sumset with the minimum size of the ordinary 2-fold sumset. Is it true that the values rho_plusminus(G, m, 2) and rho(G, m, 2) differ for fewer than n/4 choices of m?
accepted.context_brief: Frequency of disagreement for two-fold signed sumsets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 13 For any abelian group of order n, rho_plusminus(G, m, 2) and rho(G, m, 2) disagree for fewer than n/4 values of m.

accepted.question_text: For cyclic groups Z_n, determine whether the known lower bounds for the three-term restricted critical number chi_hat(Z_n, 3) are always sharp. More precisely, if n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 3 when n = p, (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 2 when n = 3p, and (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 1 otherwise? If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal floor(n/3) + 4 when 9 divides n and floor(n/3) + 3 otherwise?
accepted.context_brief: Sharpness of lower bounds for chi_hat(Z_n,3)

evidence.quote: if n >= 16 and has prime divisors congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, then chi_hat(Z_n, 3) >= (1 + 1/p) * n/3 + 3 if n = p, >= (1 + 1/p) * n/3 + 2 if n = 3p, and >= (1 + 1/p) * n/3 + 1 otherwise; and if n has no prime divisors congruent to 2 mod 3, then chi_hat(Z_n, 3) >= floor(n/3) + 4 if n is divisible by 9, and >= floor(n/3) + 3 otherwise.
We also believe that, actually, equality holds above for all n - this is certainly the case if n is even or prime; we have verified this (by computer) for all n <= 50.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For positive integers n, m, and h, is the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset in the cyclic group Z_n exactly min{u_hat(n,m,h), w_hat(n,m,h)}? Equivalently, does rho_hat(Z_n, m, h) always equal the better of the two explicit upper bounds coming from the constructions A_d(n,m) and B_d(n,m)?

evidence.quote: we see that rho_hat(Z_n, m, h) is at most min{u_hat(n, m, h), w_hat(n, m, h)}, but we also believe that equality holds: Conjecture 5 For all n, m, and h, we have rho_hat(Z_n, m, h) = min{u_hat(n, m, h), w_hat(n, m, h)}.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For every finite abelian group G, every positive integer m, and every h >= 3, does the minimum size of the h-fold signed sumset equal the explicit upper bound u_plusminus(G, m, h)? Equivalently, is rho_plusminus(G, m, h) = u_plusminus(G, m, h) always true for signed sumsets with at least three terms?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10 (Bajnok and Matzke [9]) For all G, m, and h >= 3, we have rho_plusminus(G, m, h) = u_plusminus(G, m, h).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Let p be an odd prime and consider the elementary abelian group Z_p^r. Set delta = 0 when p - 1 is divisible by h and delta = 1 otherwise. Let k be the largest integer with p^k + delta <= hm - h + 1, and let q be the largest integer with (hq + 1)p^k + delta <= hm - h + 1. If h < p and m > (q + 1)p^k, must the minimum size of the h-fold signed sumset be strictly larger than the minimum size of the ordinary h-fold sumset? Equivalently, in this remaining case not covered by Theorem 11, is rho_plusminus(Z_p^r, m, h) > rho(Z_p^r, m, h)?

evidence.quote: pk + delta <= hm - h + 1, where delta = 0 if p - 1 is divisible by h and delta = 1 otherwise. Second, set q equal to the largest integer for which (hq + 1)pk + delta <= hm - h + 1.
Conjecture 12 (Bajnok and Matzke [10]) If h < p and m > (q + 1)pk with k and q defined as above, then rho_plusminus(Z_p^r, m, h) > rho(Z_p^r, m, h).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Classify exactly when each of the three structural types of subsets of a finite abelian group - symmetric subsets, near-symmetric subsets, and asymmetric subsets - yields a signed sumset of minimum possible size. More precisely, determine for which parameters (G, m, h) each of these three types can realize |h_plusminus A| = rho_plusminus(G, m, h).

evidence.quote: This does not completely solve the inverse problem: we may have other subsets with |h_plusminus A| = rho_plusminus(G, m, h). Furthermore, it would be interesting to know exactly when each of the three types of sets just described yields a signed sumset of minimum size.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For all positive integers n and m <= n, is the minimum size of the restricted sumset with an arbitrary number of terms in the cyclic group Z_n equal to the explicit bound u(n, m, N_0)? Equivalently, does rho_hat(Z_n, m, N_0) = u(n, m, N_0) always hold?

evidence.quote: After some numerical experimentation, we believe that equality holds: Conjecture 15 For all positive integers n and m <= n, we have rho_hat(Z_n, m, N_0) = u(n, m, N_0).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Let p be a sufficiently large odd prime, and let A be a subset of Z_p of size chi_hat(Z_p, N_0) - 1 = floor(sqrt(2p - 2)). Classify exactly when the subset sums fail to cover the whole group. Is it true that Sigma A != Z_p if and only if there exists a nonzero b in Z_p such that the norm of b.A, defined by identifying Z_p with integers between -(p-1)/2 and (p-1)/2 and summing absolute values, satisfies ||b.A|| <= p - 2?

evidence.quote: We believe that this simple condition answers our inverse problem for all large enough primes; namely: there is a positive integer p0 so that if p > p0 is prime and A subset Z_p has size chi_hat(Z_p, N_0) - 1 = floor(sqrt(2p - 2)), then Sigma A != Z_p if, and only if, there is a nonzero element b in Z_p for which ||b . A|| <= p - 2.
